terms.gloss: get rid of, remove, send away
evidence: Ter. Ad. 4.2.14: ego hunc āmovēbō (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Att. 1.12: illum ex istīs locīs āmovē (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of people and things, and of feelings: āmōtō metū, fear set aside (Ter. And. 1.2.10).

terms.register: chiefly comic (Plaut., Ter.) and post-Augustan prose (Plin., Tac.); never in Cicero (Lewis & Short)
evidence: Traupman 99, 321, 377: istum molestum āmōlīrī volō, I want to get rid of that pest
terms.comment: To shift something heavy, and so to get a nuisance off one’s hands; hinc vōs āmōlīminī, clear off! (Ter. And. 4.2.24).

terms.gloss: do away with, get rid of
terms.comment: Of a thing done away with altogether (a law, a custom, a fear); first of all to lift (see lift, raise).

terms.gloss: be rid of, be freed from
terms.grammar: the passive of līberō, with ablative
evidence: Cic. Att. 6.1.10: aliquem magnā sollicitūdine līberāre (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: For “be rid of” a worry, a debt, a duty: eā cūrā līberātus sum.

phrases.english: all right, I’ll get rid of him all the same
